cross_tool_domains.attrition: Not applicable / Low concern for secondary aggregate tables: Not a longitudinal individual-level study; in comparing 2000 and 2010 IBGE municipal census totals (Table 1, PDF Page 12), the authors transparently flag boundary changes where Mesquita separated from Nova Iguaçu, precluding precise two-wave comparison for those two municipalities.
cross_tool_domains.confounding: High concern (uncontrolled descriptive case study): No design-based or statistical adjustment for structural confounders such as municipal fiscal capacity, topography, informal settlement growth rates, or historical municipal governance differences when attributing peripheral supply deficits to CEDAE's management model.
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Moderate: Accurately identifies relevant planning, regulatory, and administrative instruments—including the 2010 UN human right to water resolution, PLANSAB (2013), State Water Resources Plan (PERHI, 2014), PSAM municipal sanitation plans, ANA/ONS Paraíba do Sul reservoir operating rules, State Decree No. 40.670/2007 (APA Guandu), Brazil's Forestry Code, and CEDAE's administrative Declaration of Possibility for Supply (DPA) 3-day cistern requirement for Minha Casa Minha Vida housing—though the human right to water serves mainly as a normative lens rather than a systematically coded legal variable.
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: Moderate concern: Aggregate connection rates and bulk water flows rely on established official sources (IBGE 2000/2010 Censuses, PERHI 2014, FIRJAN 2015), whereas sub-municipal service intermittency, reservoir functionality, and operational prioritization rely on unverified technician interviews and seminar presentations rather than standardized system-wide household or hydraulic metering.
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Moderate: Strength lies in demonstrating that official binary network-connection indicators (IBGE/SNIS) mask severe multi-day intermittency (e.g., water supplied only 2–4 days per week via manual switchovers and out-of-order reservoirs), complemented by municipal census connection trends and system flow/deficit estimates (L/s); however, intermittency and water quality outcomes are documented illustratively rather than measured systematically across all metropolitan districts.
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: Moderate-to-high concern: No pre-specified protocol or qualitative coding scheme is reported; findings juxtaposed from the three authors' separate research projects selectively paraphrase interview testimony without reporting full interview counts, negative/dissenting accounts, or systematic analytical outputs.
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: Moderate-to-high concern: While macro-system and municipal census comparisons cover the metropolitan service area, qualitative semi-structured interviews with CEDAE/DAE technicians, managers, and experts lack any reported sampling frame, participant count, or recruitment criteria, and sub-municipal examples (e.g., Duque de Caxias, Queimados) are selected illustratively.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Was there a clear statement of the aims of the research?
domain_ratings.justification: The authors clearly state the objective of analyzing water supply in the Rio de Janeiro Metropolitan Area (RJMA) through the conceptual lenses of hydrosocial scarcity and the human right to water, alongside assessing whether bulk water availability aggravates access deficits, supported by five explicit research questions and a clear guiding hypothesis.

A qualitative case-study methodology combining documentary analysis of water/sanitation plans and semi-structured interviews with utility technicians and managers is appropriate for investigating socio-technical governance, operational decision-making, and lived/operational intermittency concealed by aggregate census connection figures.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Pages 2-4, Sections 1-2; PDF Page 11, Section 4.2.iv

domain_ratings.domain_name: Was the research design appropriate to address the aims of the research?
domain_ratings.justification: Following Lorrain and Poupeau's (2014) multi-source urban water governance approach, the comparative case-study design contrasting the Eastern (Imunana/Laranjal) and Western (Guandu/Lajes/Acari) macro-systems and central versus peripheral municipalities appropriately addresses the research questions, even though the mechanics of integrating the three authors' prior research streams are only briefly outlined.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Pages 2-3, Section 1 (Introduction); PDF Pages 7-18, Sections 4-5

domain_ratings.domain_name: Was the recruitment strategy appropriate to the aims of the research?
domain_ratings.justification: Although the paper cites semi-structured interviews with CEDAE and municipal DAE technicians and managers (under the EU FP7 Desafio project) as well as 2015 expert interviews, it provides no details on recruitment strategy, inclusion criteria, number of interviewees, or whether affected residents and civil-society actors were interviewed.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Pages 2-3, Section 1; PDF Page 6, Section 3.2; PDF Pages 13-15, Section 4.2.iv

domain_ratings.domain_name: Was the data collected in a way that addressed the research issue?
domain_ratings.justification: The study identifies relevant documentary sources (PERHI 2014, PLANSAB 2013, PSAM municipal sanitation plans, CEDAE and FIRJAN engineering reports, IBGE 2000/2010 censuses) and semi-structured interviews, but omits key data-collection details including interview guides, number and duration of interviews, recording/transcription methods, and documentary extraction protocols.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Pages 2-3, Section 1; PDF Pages 6, 13-15, Sections 3.2 and 4.2.iv

domain_ratings.domain_name: Has the relationship between researcher and participants been adequately considered?
domain_ratings.justification: Apart from academic biographical footnotes on PDF Page 1, the authors do not discuss researcher reflexivity, positionality, institutional relationships with CEDAE or state water agencies, or potential bias in eliciting and interpreting technician testimony.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Have ethical issues been taken into consideration?
domain_ratings.justification: Interviewed technicians and managers are anonymized by professional role in the text, which affords basic confidentiality, but there is no mention of institutional ethics approval, informed consent procedures, or ethical safeguards for human-subjects interviews.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Pages 2-3, Section 1; PDF Pages 13-15, Section 4.2.iv

domain_ratings.domain_name: Was the data analysis sufficiently rigorous?
domain_ratings.justification: The authors state only that they juxtapose research findings from the three authors across multiple sources, without describing any qualitative coding procedure, thematic analysis method, triangulation rules for conflicting evidence, or systematic criteria for selecting interview claims and municipal examples.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Pages 2-3, Section 1; PDF Pages 11-15, Section 4.2.iv

domain_ratings.domain_name: Is there a clear statement of findings?
domain_ratings.justification: Findings are clearly structured and argued across bulk water hydrology and drought management (Section 3), macro-system infrastructure and municipal service disparities (Section 4), expansion proposals (Section 5), and conclusions (Section 6), directly answering each guiding research question.

Valuable substantive contribution to urban water governance and human-right-to-water research: it demonstrates that official census network-connection rates mask severe multi-day rationing in Rio de Janeiro's metropolitan periphery, decouples the 2014-2015 Paraíba do Sul hydrological drought from chronic Baixada Fluminense supply deficits, and documents concrete institutional mechanisms of hydrosocial scarcity (such as industrial water prioritization and CEDAE's 3-day cistern requirement for social housing), though methodological opacity in interview sampling and analysis limits standalone evidentiary rigor.
domain_ratings.rating: Valuable contextual and institutional case study (tempered by weak reporting of primary qualitative methods)

overall_narrative_summary: Britto, Formiga-Johnsson, and Carneiro (2016) present a multi-source qualitative documentary and interview case study examining water supply inequalities, bulk water availability during the 2014-2015 drought, and hydrosocial scarcity in the Rio de Janeiro Metropolitan Area (RJMA). Appraised with the CASP Qualitative Checklist, the study exhibits clear research aims (Q1: Yes), an appropriate qualitative methodology (Q2: Yes) and comparative macro-system case-study design (Q3: Yes), and a coherent, well-structured statement of findings (Q9: Yes) showing that peripheral residential shortages in Baixada Fluminense, São Gonçalo, and Itaboraí stem from incomplete storage/distribution infrastructure, ~40% system losses, and industrial supply prioritization rather than Paraíba do Sul drought alone. However, methodological reporting is weak: participant recruitment (Q4: Can't tell), interview and documentary collection procedures (Q5: Can't tell), and research ethics/consent protocols (Q7: Can't tell) are insufficiently detailed, while researcher reflexivity (Q6: No) and rigorous qualitative data-analysis/coding procedures (Q8: No) are absent beyond juxtaposing prior findings from the three authors. Overall methodological concern is therefore rated Moderate-to-High (3 Can't tell and 2 No items across Q1-Q9).
overall_rating: Moderate-to-high methodological concern (3 Can't tell and 2 No items across Q1-Q9)
study_design_identified: Qualitative multi-source documentary and semi-structured interview case study (incorporating descriptive secondary census and engineering statistics)
where_found_summary: Research aims, guiding questions, hypothesis, and multi-source qualitative methodology (citing Lorrain & Poupeau 2014, planning documents, and semi-structured interviews under the EU FP7 Desafio project) are on PDF Pages 2-3 (Section 1) and PDF Page 23 (Abstract). Theoretical framing is on PDF Pages 3-4 (Section 2). Bulk water hydrology and 2014-2015 drought findings are on PDF Pages 4-7 (Section 3). Macro-system descriptions, IBGE 2000/2010 municipal connection tables, and technician interview evidence on intermittency and industrial prioritization are on PDF Pages 7-15 (Section 4). Future supply/demand projections are on PDF Pages 15-18 (Section 5), and synthesized conclusions are on PDF Pages 18-20 (Section 6).
why_tool_chosen: The study is a qualitative multi-source urban water governance case study following Lorrain and Poupeau (2014), synthesizing planning/administrative documents (PLANSAB, PERHI, PSAM municipal sanitation plans, CEDAE/FIRJAN reports) and primary semi-structured interviews with CEDAE/DAE technicians, managers, and experts. CASP Qualitative Checklist directly covers qualitative documentary and interview case studies. MMAT was not chosen because the municipal IBGE census counts (Tables 1-2) and engineering flow projections (Tables 3-4) are purely secondary descriptive background tables rather than a primary quantitative empirical study component, and the Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework is reserved for doctrinal/institutional studies fitting none of the conventional designs.
